passages.title: The Gingerbread Baker
passages.text: Mr Crumb opened his bakery forty years ago. At first he only sold bread, but one winter he made gingerbread houses for the village children. They were so popular that people came from other towns to buy them. Now his granddaughter Poppy helps him. She decorates the houses with sweets while Mr Crumb bakes. He says he will never stop working because he loves seeing children smile.

passages.title: Camping by the River
passages.text: Last weekend my family went camping by the river. On Saturday we went fishing, but we didn't catch anything! In the evening it got very cold, so we made a fire and cooked sausages. On Sunday morning it rained heavily and our tent got wet. We packed up early and drove home, but we all agreed it was a great adventure.

passages.title: The Sweet Shop Job
passages.text: Hi Ollie, guess what? I've got a Saturday job at Mrs Plum's sweet shop! I start at nine and finish at three. I help customers, put sweets into jars and clean the counter. The pay isn't great, but Mrs Plum lets me take home any broken lollipops! Last Saturday it was really busy because of the village fair. Are you free next Sunday? We could go to the lake. Love, Kit

passages.text: Hi Mum! Camp is brilliant. Yesterday we went canoeing on the lake. I fell in the water, but it was really funny and I wasn't hurt. The food is OK, but I miss your pancakes! Tomorrow we're going to climb a hill and have a picnic at the top. See you on Saturday! Love, Sam

passages.title: The School Garden
passages.text: Last spring, Class 4B started a garden behind the school. They planted tomatoes, beans and sunflowers. Every Friday, two students watered the plants. In July, the sunflowers were taller than the teacher! The class sold their tomatoes at the summer fair and used the money to buy books for the library.

passages.text: Leo's grandpa built a little robot called Robo. Robo can carry cups, water plants and tell jokes. But Robo isn't perfect. Last week he tried to water the cat! Now Grandpa is teaching Robo the difference between plants and pets. Leo thinks Robo is the best invention in the world.

passages.title: Candy Village Bake-Off
passages.text: Every year, Candy Village has a baking competition. This year, the theme was 'rainbows'. Mia made a cake with seven coloured layers. It took her five hours! Tom made rainbow cookies, but he burnt the first batch. The judges loved Mia's cake, but the prize went to old Mrs Plum for her rainbow jelly.

passages.text: Do you love stories? Join the Starlight Library Club! We meet every Wednesday from 3.30 to 4.30 p.m. in the library's Blue Room. Each week we read a short story, play word games and make bookmarks. The club is free, but please bring a snack to share. Children aged 8 to 11 only. To join, speak to Miss Rose at the front desk before Friday.

passages.title: The Missing Football
passages.text: On Monday, Kai's football disappeared from the garden. He looked everywhere: under the bushes, behind the shed and even in the pond. He was sure his neighbour's dog, Buster, had taken it. But on Thursday his little sister laughed and opened her wardrobe. The ball was inside! She had hidden it as a joke. Kai wasn't angry for long, and Buster got an extra biscuit to say sorry.

questions.q: Where did Kai NOT look?
questions.explain: He looked in the garden: bushes, shed, pond. The ball was in the house.

notes.in the pond: He even looked in the pond.

questions.q: Who did Kai think took the ball?
questions.explain: 'He was sure his neighbour's dog, Buster, had taken it.'

notes.his sister: He found out about his sister later.

questions.q: How long was the ball missing?
questions.explain: Monday to Thursday = three days.

questions.q: Why did his sister hide it?
questions.explain: 'She had hidden it as a joke.'

notes.to keep it safe: Keeping it safe isn't the reason.

questions.q: Why did Buster get a biscuit?
questions.explain: 'To say sorry': Kai blamed him, but he didn't do it.

passages.title: A Letter to Grandma
passages.text: Dear Grandma, Thank you for the telescope! Last night Dad and I took it into the garden. At first I couldn't see anything because it was cloudy. Then the clouds moved and I saw the moon. It was bigger and brighter than I expected, and I could see grey spots on it. Next week we're going to look for Jupiter. I'll tell you what I see! Love, Mina

options: to thank Grandma for a present
questions.explain: 'Thank you for the telescope!'

questions.q: Why couldn't she see anything at first?
questions.explain: 'Because it was cloudy.'

questions.explain: 'Bigger and brighter than I expected.'

notes.its colour: She saw grey spots, but colour wasn't the surprise.

questions.explain: 'Next week we're going to look for Jupiter' (a planet).

questions.q: Who used the telescope with Mina?

passages.title: Marco's Pancake Disaster
passages.text: On Sunday, Marco wanted to make pancakes for his mum's birthday. He got up early and found a recipe online. He mixed the flour, eggs and milk, but he put in salt instead of sugar! The pancakes looked perfect but tasted terrible. Marco felt awful. His mum laughed and said it was the best birthday surprise ever. Then they made a new batch together.

questions.q: How did his mum react?

passages.title: Ella's Diary: First Day at a New School
passages.text: Today was my first day at Hilltop School. I was really nervous this morning. The building is much bigger than my old school, and I got lost twice! At lunch, a girl called Priya asked me to sit with her. She likes drawing, like me. My new teacher, Mr Diaz, is strict but kind. I think I'm going to like it here.

passages.text: Every day, thousands of children around the world watch the penguins at Frostbay Zoo on a webcam. The camera is in the penguins' pool, so you can see them swim underwater. Feeding time is at 11 a.m. and 3 p.m., and it's the most popular time to watch. Last month, a baby penguin was born. The zoo asked viewers to choose its name. The winner was 'Pebble'.

passages.title: The Kindest Dragon in Candy Village
passages.text: Long ago, a dragon called Toffee lived near Candy Village. The villagers were scared of her because she was huge. One winter, the village ovens stopped working and nobody could bake bread. Toffee flew down and gently breathed fire into every oven. After that, the villagers made her a giant honey cake every year. Now children ride on her back at the spring festival.

questions.explain: 'Made her a giant honey cake every year.'

passages.title: Poster: Space Camp for Kids
passages.text: Do you love stars and planets? Come to Space Camp at Riverside Science Centre! The camp is for children aged 8 to 12 and runs from 3 to 7 August, 9 am to 3 pm. You will build a model rocket, try on a real space helmet and watch a film in our star dome. Bring a packed lunch and a water bottle. The camp costs £60, and brothers and sisters pay only £45. Book at the front desk before 20 July.

passages.title: The Hamster Who Escaped
passages.text: Last Thursday, our class hamster, Nibbles, escaped from his cage. Our teacher, Mrs Patel, forgot to close the door after she cleaned it. We looked everywhere: under the desks, behind the bookshelf and inside the bins. We couldn't find him. The next morning, Jamie opened his school bag and screamed. Nibbles was inside, eating Jamie's crisps! Now there is a lock on the cage.

questions.q: How did Nibbles get out?
questions.explain: 'Mrs Patel forgot to close the door after she cleaned it.'

notes.the cage broke: Nothing broke; the door wasn't closed.
notes.he bit through the lock: There was no lock then; it came later.

questions.q: Where did the class NOT look?
questions.explain: 'Under the desks, behind the bookshelf and inside the bins.'

questions.q: When did they find Nibbles?
questions.explain: 'Last Thursday'… 'The next morning' = Friday morning.

notes.on Thursday evening: They couldn't find him on Thursday.

questions.explain: 'Jamie opened his school bag and screamed. Nibbles was inside.'

notes.Nibbles bit him: The story doesn't say Nibbles bit him.
notes.he lost his bag: His bag was there; he opened it.
notes.Mrs Patel shouted at him: Mrs Patel doesn't shout in the story.

notes.Nibbles lives with Jamie: Nibbles was only in Jamie's bag for one night.

passages.title: Email: The Dinosaur Museum
passages.text: Hi Grandpa, Guess what? On Saturday Dad took me to the Dinosaur Museum. The T. rex skeleton was enormous, much bigger than our house! My favourite part was the dig pit, where we used brushes to find fake bones. I found a tooth! We wanted to see the flying reptile show, but it was full, so we're going to go back next month. I bought you a postcard. Love, Kayla

questions.q: Who went to the museum with Kayla?
questions.explain: 'Dad took me to the Dinosaur Museum.'

notes.her class: Her class isn't in the email.
